text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: us-west-1 Route53 health checks flapping for api.redwood.ai. Paging eng-oncall.

lina: taking this. joining channel.

alex: i'm seeing a cluster of failed healthchecks from AWS healthcheck IP ranges starting 13:42 UTC. our origin responds fine from multiple vantage points (curl 200 from eu, us-east).

mark: checking global routing, no BGP issues. some edge LB nodes reporting 503s for a small subset of client subnets but overall traffic looks fine.

lina: can someone check ingress firewall / network ACLs in us-west-1? healthchecker IPs might be getting blocked.

deploy-bot: recent infra change detected: `infra-networking apply us-west-1 acl v42` by alex at 13:40:12 UTC.

alex: ugh that was me, i pushed a tighter ACL to block a crypto-miner ASN. i thought it only affected egress to weird ASNs, but the rule order might have caught our healthchecker prefixes. reverting now.

lina: please paste revert commands and keep us updated.

alex: running:
```
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0abcd1234 --rule-number 101 --egress false --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --protocol -1 --rule-action allow
```

rachel: i've silenced Route53 pager for us-west-1 for 15m to avoid page storms while we validate. scoping to route53-health-usw1 only. :white_check_mark:

mark: post-revert, I'm seeing SYNs from healthcheck IPs reach the NLB. however a handful of healthcheck sources still show timeouts — looks like two healthcheck nodes were blackholed for ~3m. we might have also hit resolver caching returning NXDOMAIN for one edge domain; investigating.

lina: i'm running `dig +trace` from multiple regions. us-west-1 resolvers intermittently returned SERVFAIL for a subset of probes during 13:41-13:44. could be transient from our internal resolver fleet (dns-cache-nodes) being restarted around the same time. any deploys?

deploy-bot: detected job: `dns-cache rolling-restart` by rachel at 13:39:50 UTC (scheduled maintain window).

alex: oh no. so two simultaneous changes: tight ACL + dns-cache restart. healthchecks originated from AWS IPs; ACL blocked a portion; dns-cache restarts caused some resolvers to return SERVFAIL/NXDOMAIN -> Route53 healthcheck evaluation failed when it couldn't resolve origin, and others just timed out. combination = cascading false positives.

lina: summary for CS: no customer-facing 5xx spike, short p95 blip for requests routed to specific LBs (~+180ms). Most user traffic unaffected. I'll draft a conservative note.

cs-bot: Alerting CS: "We observed short-lived Route53 healthcheck flaps in us-west-1 due to concurrent network ACL change and DNS cache restarts. We have reverted the ACL and finished DNS cache restart; backend reachability restored. No customer-facing errors observed. Follow-up postmortem in progress."

mark: removing the temporary suppression in 10m to observe real healthcheck transitions. collectors report the majority of checks now passing.

alex: apologies team. immediate actions: (1) revert done; (2) I'm adding a preflight check to infra CLI to verify AWS healthcheck CIDR ranges are not denied by ACLs before apply; pushing a quick PR.

rachel: ops action: will avoid rolling restarts of dns-cache nodes during config/ACL changes in the same window. we'll sequence maintenances.

lina: handoff: i'll monitor for 30m then pass to mark. nate? (oncall rotation)

incident-bot: note recorded: ACL revert by alex; dns-cache restart was scheduled; suppression applied by rachel. Handoff to mark for watch.

mark: taking watch. setting a short dashboard alert to notify monitoring channel only if healthchecks fail for >5m.

lina: post-incident action items: (A) infra CLI preflight to forbid ACLs that would deny known AWS healthcheck CIDRs; (B) add canary to dns-cache restart job (restart 1 pod, wait 2m), (C) change route53 alerting policy to avoid paging on single-window flaps tied to DNS resolution failures, (D) update runbook to check for concurrent network and DNS changes. i'll own the doc and assign.

alex: i'll own the infra CLI PR and follow up with a changelog note.

rachel: i'll update maintenance scheduling guidelines.

(incident resolved: ACL reverted, DNS caches stabilized, Route53 healthchecks recovered, suppression removed after watch window, CS notified, postmortem actions created)
